title: Review friction map + micro-sprint lanes (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick, messy capture of recurring friction points in our PR/review flow + tiny experiment lanes we can run in 1–2 week cycles. Not a polished plan — notes to self and a few action items to try next sprint.

Context / problem statements (observed):
- Reviews for infra/runtime changes often stall at 1–2 reviewers because of contextual overhead (build matrix, perf runs). Context setup time >> diff size.
- Frontend/console PRs get micro-comments about copy/ux that circulate for days rather than quick inline fixes.
- Refactors touching shared libs create a cascade of follow-on PRs (ownership unclear).
- Merge anxiety: small risk aversion leads to bigger bundles and long review cycles.
- Async feedback loops are noisy: thread duplication in Slack + GitHub comments leads to missed TODOs.

Hypotheses (what to test):
1) Explicit "review intent" label on PRs (fast-track vs deep-review) reduces time-to-merge for low-risk changes by 30%.
2) Pre-merge lightweight annotation template (see below) reduces re-review rounds for infra changes by surfacing required checks early.
3) Designating a short-lived reviewer pool per sprint (2-3 people) lowers context-switch penalty vs ad-hoc reviewers.

Quick annotation template (copyable):
- Reviewer role: [safety|perf|api|ux]  // which signal I'm asking for
- Intent: [quick-approve|request-change|blocking-question]
- Perf: baseline job (link) + expected delta (±%)
- Risk notes: migration, DB, public API? (yes/no + brief)
- Followups: list of files to watch after merge (tests / metric alerts)

Friction map (rough lanes):
- Setup/context cost: infra + perf runs + local repro
  - Pain: reviewers spin-up time; tests ephemeral
  - Micro-sprint: keep a single perf harness VM pinned during review window; short window slot (2 days) to run baseline jobs.
- Small UX copy churn: many tiny comments
  - Pain: threads balloon, author pinged repeatedly
  - Micro-sprint: batch UX feedback into a single pass; owner consolidates and pushes patch.
- Shared-lib cascade: refactor ripple PRs
  - Pain: uncertain ownership; dependent PRs block mainline
  - Micro-sprint: owner adds "compat shim" option and files a follow-on cleanup ticket; merge with feature-flag gate.
- Merge fear -> large bundles
  - Pain: bigger surface for reviewers; longer latency
  - Micro-sprint: encourage 1-2 logical commits max + checklist for rollback plan.

Small experiments to run (1–2 week each):
A) Review-intent label pilot (week 1–2):
  - Setup: label options in repo, document usage, ask 3 teams to opt in.
  - Metrics: median time-to-merge, re-review count, number of labels misused.
  - Quick exit: if misuse > 30% cancel.
B) Annotation template + pre-checklist (week 3–4):
  - Embed template in PR description by default for infra/* and runtime/* paths via PR template change.
  - Make perf baseline link required field for runtime changes.
C) Reviewer pool rotation (ongoing):
  - Assign 2 people per sprint (opt-in), capture weekly capacity, rotate.
  - Track review latency vs ad-hoc baseline.

Ops checklist (for author before requesting review):
- [ ] PR description follows annotation template
- [ ] Minimal test matrix documented (link)
- [ ] Migration/compat note present or N/A
- [ ] Rollback plan (git revert steps) attached if > minor
- [ ] Size: split if > ~400 changed lines or > 5 logical modules

Reviewer mental model quick-guide (for reviewers):
- If intent=quick-approve and change is low-risk, prefer a fast approve + comment for follow-up rather than hold.
- If perf impact flagged: validate baseline link and spot check job logs (no need to run full suite unless delta > 10%).
- For cross-cutting refactors: decide accept+compat-shim vs hold for follow-ups. Default to accept if shim exists.

Open questions / risks:
- How to measure "misuse" vs legitimate label choices? Need manual sampling (5% of PRs) for first month.
- Are teams willing to adopt new template? Ops overhead + education cost.
- Can automation enforce template fields without friction? Explore GitHub Action to block if missing.

Immediate todos (next 7 days):
- [ ] Draft PR template change and push to repo (me) — target: Monday
- [ ] Slack note in #dev-reviews asking for 3 teams to trial label — target: Tuesday (Ana to co-signal)
- [ ] Small GH Action prototype to require perf link on runtime paths (Marcus)
- [ ] Capture baseline metrics for past 30 days: median TTMs and avg review rounds (data request to eng-analytics)

Notes-to-self (random):
- Keep experiment scope tight: one micro-sprint per friction lane; measure, iterate.
- If reviewer pool reduces latency but increases unfair load, make it opt-in with rotation and on-call credits.
- Consider adding a short video (2m) showing how to fill the annotation template; people skip docs otherwise.

Examples / quick snippets to copy into PR template:
> Reviewer role: perf
> Intent: quick-approve
> Perf baseline: https://perf.redwood-inference/internal/job/abc123 (delta expected: +1%)
> Risk: DB migration? no
> Followups: monitor redis_conn_established gauge for 48h

Reference links (for later):
- Confluence: Review-runbook / PR conventions (placeholder)
- GH: repo templates path: .github/pull_request_template.md
- Infra perf harness: https://internal-tools.redwood/perf-harness

End note:
This is messy. Focus experiments on reducing reviewer start-time (context cost) and on surfacing perf/rollback signals early. If we get even 15% reduction in median TTM for infra/runtime PRs, that's enough to scale the approach.

-- Sam R.
